book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: Should new capital buy EQT at $52.81 today, or wait for the $48.00–$50.50 support shelf?

epigraph.quote: Great businesses at mediocre prices or broken charts test your patience; great setups reward it.
epigraph.author: Institutional Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: What EQT Does: EQT Corporation (NYSE: EQT) is North America's premier integrated natural gas major [1, 2]. It produces ~2.1+ Tcfe annually from 28.0 Tcfe of proved Appalachian reserves (93% Marcellus) [1, 2]. Its owned Equitrans Midstream gathering network and 2.0 Bcf/d Mountain Valley Pipeline move those molecules to market [1, 2]. In 2024, EQT integrated its $14B Equitrans deal [1]. By Q3 2026, it cut net debt to $5.5B [28]. On October 26, 2026, it announced a $13B–$14B all-stock deal for Range Resources at a 0.987x exchange ratio [26]. Today, EQT runs at a ~$2.00/MMBtu unlevered FCF breakeven [1, 26, 28].

web_blocks.takeaway: EQT is a Tier-2 cyclical leader to accumulate on a pullback to $48.00–$50.50 (or on a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above $55.50), not chased at $52.81 [23].

web_blocks.html: Bull vs. Bear in Two Sentences: Bulls cite EQT's $1.03–$1.09/Mcfe operating cost, $325M–$600M Range synergies, and multi-year LNG/AI power demand [1, 26, 28]. Bears point to EIA's $2.88/MMBtu 2027 Henry Hub forecast, Permian associated-gas supply, and 27% Range equity dilution [25, 26]. They also note a weak chart below the 200-DMA [23]. Our independent view: wait for $48.00–$50.50, where risk-reward tilts in our favor.

book_paragraphs: Picture a company that controls the lowest-cost natural gas molecules on the North American continent, owns the gathering pipes that collect them, owns the interstate pipeline that carries them out of Appalachia, and just generated $2.80 billion of free cash flow in a single year—yet its stock sits 22.6% below its 52-week high.

That is the puzzle of EQT Corporation at $52.81 on November 13, 2026. Over the next nine chapters, you and I are going to strip away the Wall Street slogans and underwrite this business from the rock up—first completely blind to the stock price, then testing what the market is actually pricing in.

Here is our bottom line up front, earned after the full ten-chapter audit: EQT earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality rating with all six leading operational KPIs passing. Yet our New-Capital Verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT, and our Holding Action is NOT_HELD (zero shares owned). At $52.81, EQT trades below both its 30-week ($53.47) and 200-day ($55.48) moving averages during a broader US Market Correction, offering only 1.35-to-1 reward-to-risk to our $64.00 Base Case target. By exercising patience for our $48.00–$50.50 support shelf—with a hard invalidation stop at $44.50—our asymmetry jumps to 2.25-to-1. Keep your cash in T-bills until the tape or the price meets our terms.

Think of this monograph as a permanent field manual for EQT Corporation: every number is tied to an audited SEC filing, a verified November 13, 2026 market snapshot, or a primary operational release, and every judgment is separated cleanly into business quality first, valuation and tape second. Whether EQT hits our $48.00–$50.50 support shelf this winter or stages a high-volume breakout above $55.50 after closing Range Resources, you now know exactly what you own, what it is worth, and what price demands action.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good underwriting separates 'great operator' from 'buy right now.' EQT's management has built an enviable gas-and-pipe fortress, but disciplined capital waits for asymmetric odds.

book_subsections.title: How to Use This Dossier: The Two-Pass Underwriting Method
paragraphs: Before we dive into Chapter 1, notice how this monograph is built. Too many stock reports start with a price target and work backward, cherry-picking bullish anecdotes to justify a predetermined rating. Here, you and I do the exact opposite: Chapters 1 through 6 were written completely blind to EQT's stock price, valuation multiples, and chart—forcing us to judge the rock, the pipes, the unit economics, and management's ten-year cash record on their own merits.

Only after locking our business quality verdict (CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL, with all six leading KPIs passing) did we unlock the live November 13, 2026 market tape ($52.81) in Chapters 7 through 9. That separation is your best defense against narrative bias and FOMO.
